Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Search Submit Search Close Search Toggle Menu Academics Majors, Minors and Certificates Online Degrees and Programs Pre-Med and Pre-Health Programs Pre-Law Preparation Graduate College Veterinary Medicine Admission and Aid Admissions Tuition and Fees Affording College New Student Programs Apply Request Information Visit Meet Your Admissions Counselor Virtual Office For Admitted Students Be a Student Leader Learn by Doing Career Preparation Honors Program Industry Partners Innovation and Entrepreneurship Research Study Abroad Life at Iowa State You Belong Here Learning Communities Campus and Ames Housing and Dining Health and Safety Athletics and Recreation Activities and Involvement Academic Support History and Traditions MyAccount Request Info Apply Visit Give Research Extension Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Submit Search Home Admission and Aid Admissions International Students Admitted International Undergraduate Students For Admitted International Undergraduate Students International Students International First-Year Requirements International Transfer Requirements English Proficiency Requirement Admitted International Undergraduate Students International Student Excellence Award International Merit Scholarships STEM Optional Practical Training Frequently Asked Questions International Student Ambassadors FAM Visit Program STEAM Innovation Academy We know a Cyclone when we see one Welcome to Iowa State! Congratulations on your admission – we’re thrilled to have you join the Cyclone community! Your future is in the making. Accept your offer of admission Accept your offer of admission Accept your offer of admission by submitting the $425 acceptance fee, before July 1. This crucial step ensures you stay on track to access important next steps, including the on-campus housing contract and essential online orientation materials, such as course registration, early arrival housing, health records, and more. Failure to accept your offer of admission by July 1 may lead to the offer being revoked. Refund policy for visa denial If your visa application is denied, you may request a partial refund of the acceptance fee in the amount of $365. To initiate your refund, email admissions@iastate.edu with your request. Apply for scholarships (optional) The Office of Admissions offers a range of scholarships for international undergraduate students. Students must receive admission to Iowa State to be eligible for scholarships. International Excellence Award ($10,000-$12,000/year) This scholarship is automatically awarded to first-year international students based on their GPA and SAT/ACT scores. For automatic scholarship consideration, upload your SAT/ACT scores to your Admissions MyAccount. International Merit Scholarship ($4,000 or $10,000) First-year and transfer students may apply for this scholarship through Iowa State University’s OneApp Scholarship Application. To apply, complete the general OneApp application and the separate International Admissions Scholarship application for your entry term, available under “recommended opportunities”. Note that the International Excellence Award cannot be combined with the International Merit Scholarship. Additionally, Iowa State's academic colleges and departments offer further scholarship opportunities that may be combined with either of the scholarships mentioned above. Students are encouraged to explore these additional scholarship opportunities through the OneApp. Submit your housing contract (optional) Iowa State has a variety of on-campus housing options for students. Your housing assignment is based off the date you submit your housing contract and is made on a first-come, first-serve basis. You can make adjustments to your contract later, for example, adding a roommate or learning community. Receive your university ID number and create your Net-ID After being admitted to Iowa State, you will receive your 9-digit university ID number. Be sure to keep this number on hand, as it will be used throughout your arrival process. Your Net-ID serves as your Iowa State University username which you will use to access Iowa State accounts and web applications, such as your Iowa State email. Receive your SEVIS I-20 (For F-1 visa applicants) To receive your I-20 form, please ensure all admissions documents, including your passport and financial documents, are submitted to the Office of Admissions via your Admissions MyAccount. If you have not yet received your I-20 or have additional questions, you may contact the Office of Admissions. Submitting your visa application After completing payment for your I-901 fee, you are ready to proceed with your visa application. To do this, you will need to Complete a DS-160 visa application form on the U.S. Department of State website. You will need information from your I-20 to complete this form. If you do not have your own contact person in the U.S., you can use the following information to complete the section of U.S. Point of Contact Information . Name: Becca Duncan Address: 2229 Lincoln Way, STE 4530, Ames, IA 50014 Phone: 515-294-1120 Email: brduncan@iastate.edu Once your DS-160 is complete, you can schedule your visa appointment at your nearby U.S. Embassy or Consulate. Please note, each Embassy manages the process of scheduling an interview differently, so please read the information on your specific Embassy location’s website carefully. Visit the ISSO Immigration and Travel webpage for detailed instructions. SEVIS transfer process for F1 visa holders currently attending a U.S. institution If you are currently studying in the U.S. on a valid F-1 visa, a SEVIS transfer I-20 / DS-2019 Form will be issued AFTER your current institution releases your SEVIS record to Iowa State (the release date is usually on or after the last day of classes). If you are a SEVIS transfer in student, you must complete the SEVIS Transfer to Iowa State University e-Form in CyStart. Login to CyStart through the “New and Former International Students and Scholars” on the right side of the screen. If you have registered your Iowa State University Net-ID, then use your Net-ID and password to login. If you have not yet registered your University Net-ID, then you will need to request a PIN through the link at the bottom of the screen that says “E-mail me my Limited Access PIN.” Once receiving the pin by email, finish logging into the page. Select “Student Services” on the left side of the page. Select “SEVIS Transfer to Iowa State University”. This form must be completed by you and the International Student Advisor at your current institution before your Iowa State University SEVIS transfer I-20 can be issued. Visit the ISSO International Transfer Students webpage for detailed information. Prepare for orientation and enrollment (Pre-arrival and new student onboarding) Approximately three months before the start the semester, the International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) will email you a pre-arrival guide which includes important information about temporary housing, registering for orientation, necessary tasks for class registration, immunization requirements, and more. You will also receive instructions to complete onboarding requirements for the Workday Student system. You are required to complete the following onboarding requirements before attending orientation and attending class. Questions regarding orientation and or the pre-arrival guide, please contact ISSO at isorient@iastate.edu . Submit your official academic records Your high school counselor may submit your academic records via the Common App or email them directly to etranscripts@iastate.edu . Also, upon your arrival to campus, you may provide a physical copy of your official records. Please note that for a physical copy to be considered official, it must be issued by the institution and include the official stamp and signature. Photocopies will not be accepted as official unless they are certified by the institution. Reserve your airport shuttle to campus and travel to Des Moines (DSM) The International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) partners with University Transportation Services to offer a free shuttle service for new international undergraduate students from Des Moines International Airport (DSM) to Ames, Iowa. This service is available up to one week before the mandatory arrival date. To reserve your shuttle, please refer to the instructions outlined by ISSO in the pre-arrival guide. Attend New Student Orientation As a new international Cyclone, you are required to attend New Student Orientation. This program, presented by the International Students and Scholars Office, is designed to help you acclimate to campus life and introduce you to the international community at Iowa State. During orientation, you will: Complete your required immigration processing with an ISSO international advisor (mandatory) Meet with your academic advisor to finalize your registration for your first-semester classes Learn about campus resources and important information about Iowa State Make new friends through ISSO social events and Destination Iowa State Take part in Destination Iowa State Destination Iowa State is an action-packed event for new students, held before the fall and spring semesters. Connect with new students and team up with an experienced team leader. Explore the campus and find your favorite spots. Prepare for classes by locating classrooms and learning about technology. Experience traditions like Hilton Magic and meeting Cy. Discover resources to stay safe and well. Join Cyclone Nation and tap into the Iowa State community. Connect with the International Students and Scholars Office The International Students and Scholars Office is dedicated to providing international scholars and students with the support, resources, and guidance they need to excel both academically and personally during their time at Iowa State. You will also learn more about the next steps in your journey to Iowa State University. Reception information Questions? The Office of Admissions is here to help. Accept your offer of admission Accept your offer of admission Accept your offer of admission by submitting the $425 acceptance fee, before July 1. This crucial step ensures you stay on track to access important next steps, including the on-campus housing contract and essential online orientation materials, such as course registration, early arrival housing, health records, and more. Failure to accept your offer of admission by July 1 may lead to the offer being revoked. Refund policy for visa denial If your visa application is denied, you may request a partial refund of the acceptance fee in the amount of $365. To initiate your refund, email admissions@iastate.edu with your request. Apply for scholarships (optional) The Office of Admissions offers a range of scholarships for international undergraduate students. Students must receive admission to Iowa State to be eligible for scholarships. International Excellence Award ($10,000-$12,000/year) This scholarship is automatically awarded to first-year international students based on their GPA and SAT/ACT scores. For automatic scholarship consideration, upload your SAT/ACT scores to your Admissions MyAccount. International Merit Scholarship ($4,000 or $10,000) First-year and transfer students may apply for this scholarship through Iowa State University’s OneApp Scholarship Application. To apply, complete the general OneApp application and the separate International Admissions Scholarship application for your entry term, available under “recommended opportunities”. Note that the International Excellence Award cannot be combined with the International Merit Scholarship. Additionally, Iowa State's academic colleges and departments offer further scholarship opportunities that may be combined with either of the scholarships mentioned above. Students are encouraged to explore these additional scholarship opportunities through the OneApp. Submit your housing contract (optional) Iowa State has a variety of on-campus housing options for students. Your housing assignment is based off the date you submit your housing contract and is made on a first-come, first-serve basis. You can make adjustments to your contract later, for example, adding a roommate or learning community. Receive your university ID number and create your Net-ID After being admitted to Iowa State, you will receive your 9-digit university ID number. Be sure to keep this number on hand, as it will be used throughout your arrival process. Your Net-ID serves as your Iowa State University username which you will use to access Iowa State accounts and web applications, such as your Iowa State email. Receive your SEVIS I-20 (For F-1 visa applicants) To receive your I-20 form, please ensure all admissions documents, including your passport and financial documents, are submitted to the Office of Admissions via your Admissions MyAccount. If you have not yet received your I-20 or have additional questions, you may contact the Office of Admissions. Submitting your visa application After completing payment for your I-901 fee, you are ready to proceed with your visa application. To do this, you will need to Complete a DS-160 visa application form on the U.S. Department of State website. You will need information from your I-20 to complete this form. If you do not have your own contact person in the U.S., you can use the following information to complete the section of U.S. Point of Contact Information . Name: Becca Duncan Address: 2229 Lincoln Way, STE 4530, Ames, IA 50014 Phone: 515-294-1120 Email: brduncan@iastate.edu Once your DS-160 is complete, you can schedule your visa appointment at your nearby U.S. Embassy or Consulate. Please note, each Embassy manages the process of scheduling an interview differently, so please read the information on your specific Embassy location’s website carefully. Visit the ISSO Immigration and Travel webpage for detailed instructions. SEVIS transfer process for F1 visa holders currently attending a U.S. institution If you are currently studying in the U.S. on a valid F-1 visa, a SEVIS transfer I-20 / DS-2019 Form will be issued AFTER your current institution releases your SEVIS record to Iowa State (the release date is usually on or after the last day of classes). If you are a SEVIS transfer in student, you must complete the SEVIS Transfer to Iowa State University e-Form in CyStart. Login to CyStart through the “New and Former International Students and Scholars” on the right side of the screen. If you have registered your Iowa State University Net-ID, then use your Net-ID and password to login. If you have not yet registered your University Net-ID, then you will need to request a PIN through the link at the bottom of the screen that says “E-mail me my Limited Access PIN.” Once receiving the pin by email, finish logging into the page. Select “Student Services” on the left side of the page. Select “SEVIS Transfer to Iowa State University”. This form must be completed by you and the International Student Advisor at your current institution before your Iowa State University SEVIS transfer I-20 can be issued. Visit the ISSO International Transfer Students webpage for detailed information. Prepare for orientation and enrollment (Pre-arrival and new student onboarding) Approximately three months before the start the semester, the International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) will email you a pre-arrival guide which includes important information about temporary housing, registering for orientation, necessary tasks for class registration, immunization requirements, and more. You will also receive instructions to complete onboarding requirements for the Workday Student system. You are required to complete the following onboarding requirements before attending orientation and attending class. Questions regarding orientation and or the pre-arrival guide, please contact ISSO at isorient@iastate.edu . Submit your official academic records Your high school counselor may submit your academic records via the Common App or email them directly to etranscripts@iastate.edu . Also, upon your arrival to campus, you may provide a physical copy of your official records. Please note that for a physical copy to be considered official, it must be issued by the institution and include the official stamp and signature. Photocopies will not be accepted as official unless they are certified by the institution. Reserve your airport shuttle to campus and travel to Des Moines (DSM) The International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) partners with University Transportation Services to offer a free shuttle service for new international undergraduate students from Des Moines International Airport (DSM) to Ames, Iowa. This service is available up to one week before the mandatory arrival date. To reserve your shuttle, please refer to the instructions outlined by ISSO in the pre-arrival guide. This program, presented by the International Students and Scholars Office, is designed to help you acclimate to campus life and introduce you to the international community at Iowa State. Connect with the International Students and Scholars Office The International Students and Scholars Office is dedicated to providing international scholars and students with the support, resources, and guidance they need to excel both academically and personally during their time at Iowa State. Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Search Submit Search Close Search Toggle Menu Academics Majors, Minors and Certificates Online Degrees and Programs Pre-Med and Pre-Health Programs Pre-Law Preparation Graduate College Veterinary Medicine Admission and Aid Admissions Tuition and Fees Affording College New Student Programs Apply Request Information Visit Meet Your Admissions Counselor Virtual Office For Admitted Students Be a Student Leader Learn by Doing Career Preparation Honors Program Industry Partners Innovation and Entrepreneurship Research Study Abroad Life at Iowa State You Belong Here Learning Communities Campus and Ames Housing and Dining Health and Safety Athletics and Recreation Activities and Involvement Academic Support History and Traditions MyAccount Request Info Apply Visit Give Research Extension Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Submit Search Home Admission and Aid Admissions International Students International Transfer Requirements American Degree Transfer Program American Degree Transfer Program – Malaysia International Transfer Requirements American Degree Transfer Program Where a Cyclone's path begins For Malaysian institutions: INTI University College, Methodist College Kuala Lumpur, Sunway University, and Taylor's University College The American Degree Transfer Program (ADTP) provides a unique pathway, allowing students to transfer to top universities, such as Iowa State University. Modeled after the American undergraduate degree program, ADTP offers a blend of major-specific and general education courses, ensuring students are well-prepared for the next phase of their studies. Students will spend approximately 12-24 months (full-time) at an ADTP university and another 24-36 months (full-time) at the university they will complete their degree, whether in the USA, Canada, or other locations. While most students complete around 60 credits in ADTP before transferring overseas to finish their degrees, it is not mandatory to reach this credit threshold before transferring. Potential majors There are more than 100 majors available. Students can choose any field of study to major in whether in art-related fields, business, social sciences or “Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics” (STEM) fields. Popular majors include: Actuarial science Business Communication Computer science Engineering Liberal arts Natural sciences Psychology ADTP International Transfer Student Award For students entering Fall 2026 and onward International students transferring from INTI University College, Methodist College Kuala Lumpur, Sunway University, and Taylor's University College, who have been offered admission, will be automatically awarded a $4,000/year stackable award. Award Duration: Up to 6 semesters or until degree completion Stackable: Can be combined with International Student Excellence or International Merit Scholarships, if eligible Award Requirements Total value Annual value Stackable? ADTP International Transfer Student Award 3.00+ transfer GPA $12,000 $4,000 (up to 3 years) Yes ADTP LAS Scholarship (Computer Science and other College of Liberal Arts and Sciences majors) 3.00+ transfer GPA $6,000 $2,000 (up to 3 years) Yes Eligibility International students transferring from the listed institutions and offered admission Accept offer by May 1 (fall) or December 15 (spring) Automatic scholarship — no separate application required Only available to students assessed international tuition Renewal requirements Maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 while enrolled at Iowa State Remain continuously enrolled in at least 12 semester credits each semester (summer not included) Only available to students assessed international tuition Award applies only to undergraduate tuition and fees Your future in the making Recommended tracks for business, computer science, and engineering are coming soon. In the meantime, click on your institution for transfer agreements. INTI University College Methodist College Kuala Lumpur Sunway University Taylor's University College Hear from Gagan and Preethi, transfer students from INTI International University. I loved that my advisors, both in MCKL ADTP and at Iowa State, were very helpful. They worked with me to maximize my transfer credits. I couldn’t have picked a better college to transfer to! Phoebe, Methodist College Kuala Lumpur (MCKL) transfer student Phoebe completed the American Degree Transfer Program through Methodist College Kuala Lumpur (MCKL). She transferred around 45 credits from MCKL to Iowa State. Find out more about her experience as a Cyclone. Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Search Submit Search Close Search Toggle Menu Academics Majors, Minors and Certificates Online Degrees and Programs Pre-Med and Pre-Health Programs Pre-Law Preparation Graduate College Veterinary Medicine Admission and Aid Admissions Tuition and Fees Affording College New Student Programs Apply Request Information Visit Meet Your Admissions Counselor Virtual Office For Admitted Students Be a Student Leader Learn by Doing Career Preparation Honors Program Industry Partners Innovation and Entrepreneurship Research Study Abroad Life at Iowa State You Belong Here Learning Communities Campus and Ames Housing and Dining Health and Safety Athletics and Recreation Activities and Involvement Academic Support History and Traditions MyAccount Request Info Apply Visit Give Research Extension Current Students Faculty and Staff Parents and Families Sign Ons Search Submit Search Home Admission and Aid Admissions International Students FAM Visit Program FAM Visit Program International Students International First-Year Requirements International Transfer Requirements English Proficiency Requirement Admitted International Undergraduate Students International Student Excellence Award International Merit Scholarships STEM Optional Practical Training Frequently Asked Questions International Student Ambassadors FAM Visit Program STEAM Innovation Academy Global connections begin here Each year, Iowa State University welcomes international high school counselors and educational partners from around the world to campus for a unique Familiarization (FAM) Visit Program. This immersive, multi-day experience offers guests the opportunity to explore our vibrant campus, engage with faculty and current students, and learn about our academic programs, student support services, and the Iowa State difference. The FAM Visit Program highlights Iowa State’s commitment to global outreach and helps strengthen relationships that support international student success. The FAM Visit Program typically takes place in June of each year. Previous slide Next slide Testimonials Rustem Capkin “From the warm hospitality to the thoughtfully curated sessions, every moment provided valuable insights into the university’s unique culture and its commitment to student success. I especially appreciated the opportunity to engage directly with faculty, staff, and current students—it offered a genuine sense of community and collaboration. This visit not only deepened my understanding of what the university offers but also strengthened my confidence in recommending it to future students." Turkey June 2025 Karen Bauer “Iowa State University offers more than just top-tier academics and impressive facilities. What stood out most was the genuine sense of community and the welcoming spirit from faculty, staff, and students. The attention to detail across campus and the strong support for international students make it a truly special place. I left inspired and grateful, and I am happy to recommend Iowa State to students across the Middle East and Central Asia.” United Arab Emirates June 2025 Lewis Cardenas “A standout moment from our Iowa State visit was a powerful project where students design footwear for people with disabilities. We had the chance to try a small version of the activity, and it was incredibly moving. It reflected Iowa State’s deep commitment to inclusive, purposeful innovation.” India August 2024 David Turner "I often encourage students and parents to have a hard look at Iowa State University. Their learning community stands apart as a forerunner for offering top-notch, relevant educational and study abroad programs, research opportunities, and so much more. With my own visit, I found the university at an interesting intersection: Iowa State is one of the largest public research universities in the United States having a number of truly big school amenities, yet it is nestled within the welcoming and vibrant small-town community of Ames, Iowa. A true gem!" United Arab Emirates December 2022 Himanshu Dev "I've been advising students to Iowa State for over a decade. Walking around the campus, eating homemade ice cream, witnessing the giant robots in labs, meeting student start-up founders, seeing flight simulations, enjoying the athletic arena, and so on – it all boosted the interest, making Iowa State a favorite. The admissions team is so detail-oriented and always available for the students. Each of my students and their families are so happy." India June 2024 Jack Zissler “Having been on many fam trips in my career, I can honestly attest to my ISU FAM experience to being absolutely terrific. From the detailed planning, fun and engaging activities, personal attention given to all attendees, and top-notch travel arrangements, this trip was far and above others I have experienced.
